clue.text: No little girl reported to have special knowledge

indicators.note: reported means the words are to be heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: a little girl is a SIS, short for sister, so the phrase gives NO SIS

explanation.surface: A gossip claims some young girl lacks any particular insight.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, NO SIS matches the first sound of the word, whose G is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is the Greek word for knowledge, used for esoteric spiritual insight possessed by initiates.

clue.text: Bread service coming to the rescue in middle of dinner

indicators.note: in tells us the service's letters sit inside the other piece
middle of picks the central pair of letters of the word dinner

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British breakdown service that rescues stranded drivers

explanation.surface: A breakdown crew arrives mid-meal with a basket of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, whose patrols rescue broken-down motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of leavened flatbread from South Asian cuisine, often served with curry.

clue.text: Queen Victoria perhaps first seen in shop

indicators.note: first says the Victoria piece comes ahead of the queen piece in the answer

parts.note: Victoria is one example of a London railway station
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The old queen herself is spotted browsing in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Victoria' reads as one monarch; split it: ER, then Victoria as a London rail terminus, put first.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer of paper, pens and office supplies is someone you would find behind the counter of a shop.

clue.text: Don't go with boy crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the boy's letters straddle, enclosing, the river

parts.note: a boy is a son
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A parent begs a lad not to leave as he wades across a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain where you are rather than leaving is a plea not to go.

clue.text: Bathroom item made of wood with roll going round

indicators.note: going round means the outer pieces surround the wood

parts.note: to bowl is to roll a ball, as on a bowling green
ash is a timber tree and its wood

explanation.surface: Describes a wooden bathroom fitting with something rolled around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of' is a link word; 'with' gives W, and 'going round' has the outer pieces surround the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin for washing hands and face is a standard fixture of a bathroom.

clue.text: The unfolding of two adrift with Gogo in

definitions.text: The unfolding of two adrift with Gogo in

indicators.note: unfolding means the following letters are opened out and laid in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of Beckett's play in which two tramps wait aimlessly, Gogo among them.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO ADRIFT plus GOGO IN, opened out ('The unfolding of'), give the title; the clue also sums up the play, in which two vagrants, Vladimir and Estragon (nicknamed Gogo), drift through events.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's play unfolds around two drifting tramps, one of them called Gogo by his companion.

clue.text: As one with evil influence, I will follow girl behind an old coach

indicators.note: behind places the girl after the coach in the answer
will follow puts the I at the end, after the other pieces

parts.note: Sven-Goran Eriksson was a former England football manager
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone sinister trails a girl who walks behind a former football manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Sven-Goran Eriksson coached the England football team from 2001 to 2006. The definition reads as 'as one with evil influence, I...', so the answer stands for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The hypnotist in du Maurier's Trilby gave his name to anyone who manipulates another with sinister control.

clue.text: Jolly good support and very little opposition, initially

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
V is the little abbreviation for very

indicators.note: initially picks just the opening letter of opposition

explanation.surface: Praise for a team that gave firm support and met little resistance early on.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of approval, like a cheer of well done.

clue.text: It goes higher if you have more in the bank

definitions.text: It goes higher if you have more in the bank

parts.words: It goes higher if you have more in the bank
parts.note: reads like savings in a bank account, but the bank is a river bank and the more is more water

explanation.definitionFit: The height of a river's surface rises when more water fills between its banks.

clue.text: I shove a resin back in dish

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: to ram is to shove forcefully
lac is a resin secreted by insects, used in shellac

explanation.surface: A cook admits forcing tree sap into a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I shove a resin' reads as a sentence about sap; 'back' reverses the entire string of pieces, and 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid served as food, usually battered and fried rings, is a familiar restaurant dish.

clue.text: Demands made by laws no longer in force?

parts.note: ex- means former, so something no longer in force
acts of parliament are laws

explanation.surface: Asks whether old statutes still make claims on people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'laws no longer in force' as former acts, ex-acts.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain, as payment or obedience; third person verb.

clue.text: Support here for an evening activity

definitions.text: Support here for an evening activity

parts.words: Support here for an evening activity
parts.note: an evening activity seems to be a night out, but evening means making even, smoothing out creases

explanation.definitionFit: A padded stand holds clothes flat while creases are pressed out with a hot iron.

clue.text: Dublin has cooked English and Continental food

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared afresh in another arrangement

explanation.surface: An Irish capital rustles up an English meal and something from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-veined cheese from Denmark, a food from continental Europe.

clue.text: Gladly pretend for those listening

indicators.note: for those listening says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to feign is to pretend

explanation.surface: An audience is happy to play along with a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: Fain is an archaic adverb meaning willingly or with pleasure.

clue.text: Waterproof items the woman's put on to travel round a lake

indicators.note: put on means the woman's piece is added after the rest
round means the travel word encloses the other letters

parts.note: to go is to travel
the woman's is she's, meaning she has

explanation.surface: A woman pulls on rain boots to walk around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber overshoes worn over ordinary shoes to keep feet dry are waterproof items.

clue.text: Unfriendly instruction? It could be the making of me

definitions.meaning: a hold-up man's command to raise your hands

definitions.text: It could be the making of me
definitions.meaning: read as an instruction for this down light: take the letters E and M and stick them upward, which spells the clue's last word

explanation.surface: A mugger's gruff command, presented as the thing that could make a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer as an order: in a down entry, sticking E M up reverses it to give 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber's command to raise hands is hardly a friendly order.

clue.text: One may offer a bit of salaciousness to person having day out

definitions.text: One may offer a bit of salaciousness to person having day out

indicators.note: a bit of takes only the opening letter of salaciousness

parts.note: a tripper is a day tripper, someone on an excursion

explanation.surface: An entertainer offers something racy to a day-trip visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic dancer who undresses offers a racy show to audiences such as holidaymakers.

clue.text: Messy blotter covering one text

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
messy says the letters are in disarray and must be reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A smudged blotting pad lies over a written page.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOTTER, rearranged ('Messy'), becomes LBRETTO, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of an opera, written as a text for the music.

clue.text: Murders in America increase regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of increase

explanation.surface: Killing rates in the United States are steadily rising.
explanation.walkthrough: To ice someone is American slang for killing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for kills, in American gangster usage, matching murders as a verb.

clue.text: One who painted peasants in the grass

definitions.meaning: Jean-Francois ..., the French painter of The Gleaners and other rural labour scenes
a cereal grass grown for its small seeds

explanation.definitionFit: Shares its name with a cereal grass and with the French artist famed for scenes of peasant life.

clue.text: Key person in society joint is very bright

indicators.note: in places the key person inside the society-and-joint pieces

parts.note: a hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg, or a joint of meat
a kingpin is the most important person in a group

explanation.surface: A leading socialite's party is dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid, garish pink colour, so bright it startles the eye.

clue.text: Resin that's hard or soft embedded in underground deposit

indicators.note: embedded in means the letter is set within the deposit word

parts.note: coal is mined from underground seams
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Asks whether a resin found in a mine is hard or soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word; the definition takes 'hard' with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard tropical tree resin used in varnishes.

clue.text: Zeus's son 'urries

definitions.meaning: the Greek god of war, a son of Zeus and Hera
hurries said with a dropped h, as in Cockney speech: hares becomes the answer

explanation.walkthrough: To hare is to rush, so 'urries is hares with the H dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The god of war in Greek myth was a son of Zeus; dropping the h from a word for rushes gives the same letters.

clue.text: Excellent drink in first half of meal

indicators.note: in puts the drink inside the shortened meal
first half of keeps only the opening three letters of the meal word, dropping the rest

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A drink served at the start of supper is a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is lavish and first-rate, so the adjective means excellent.

clue.text: Man about to join in venture as a writer

indicators.note: to join in means the man's letters go into the venture word

parts.note: to dare is to venture

indicators.note: about means the man word is turned back to front

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A fellow is about to take part in a daring enterprise as an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the man word, and 'to join in' sets it inside the venture word; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet and novelist, author of The Listeners.

clue.text: The Spanish wine taken outside its normal home?

definitions.text: The Spanish wine taken outside its normal home?

indicators.note: taken outside means the wine's letters go around the article

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
el is the Spanish definite article, the

explanation.surface: Asks where wine ends up when it leaves the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken outside' has the wine go round the Spanish article; the whole clue describes a sideboard cabinet that holds wine away from the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard for keeping wine in a dining room, outside the cellar.

clue.text: Asian drunk, reported office worker

indicators.note: reported says the phrase is to be heard spoken aloud

parts.note: a Thai is someone from Thailand, and pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A gossip says an Asian man is drunk at his office job.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed is British slang for drunk; spoken, Thai pissed sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerical worker who types letters and documents in an office.
